bug_description.normalized: The staged vulnerable checkout and saved ASan trace are FFmpeg commit `0dea0114fb29a8c533d7c36f20df7a7440605758`; the staged `sample_info.json` metadata and `patch.diff` describe an unrelated Opus change and are not the causal oracle for this sample. The exact 47-byte AAC_FIXED witness reaches `read_sbr_extension()`'s `EXTENSION_ID_PS` case, and `ff_ps_read_data_fixed()` materializes PS header state (`nr_iid_par`, `iid_quant`, `nr_icc_par`, `num_env`) plus persistent per-envelope `ps->iid_par` / `ps->icc_par` arrays. In this checkout, directly decoded IID/ICC rows are range-checked by `read_iid_data()` and `read_icc_data()`, and the later `remap20()` / `remap34()` helpers in `stereo_processing()` only copy or average the stored arrays into local `iid_mapped` / `icc_mapped` values. `ff_sbr_apply_fixed()` then takes the active-PS branch, `stereo_processing()` remaps the stored PS state, and it indexes `H_LUT` with `iid_mapped[e][b] + 7 + 23 * ps->iid_quant` and `icc_mapped[e][b]` without a sink-side bounds check. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 4-byte global-buffer-overflow at `libavcodec/aacps.c:904`. Because `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, the staged artifacts do not reveal which stored PS row/slot produced the bad mapped pair or whether it came through the fake-envelope repair path, an untouched `source < 0` synthetic row, or other earlier persisted PS state; this GT therefore keeps that earlier producer explicitly unresolved.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the witness as a Parametric Stereo payload and updates persistent `sbr->ps` state later used by `stereo_processing()`.

Reaching this call means the SBR extension dispatcher took `case EXTENSION_ID_PS` for bytes from that same bitstream.

root_cause.description: Concrete obligation gap proven by the staged source and ASan trace: `stereo_processing()` turns remapped PS IID/ICC values into `H_LUT` row and column indices and dereferences the hardcoded `[46][8][4]` table without checking that the computed pair stays within bounds.
root_cause.note: The saved run proves that one mapped IID/ICC pair reached this lookup out of range. With runtime disambiguation disabled, the staged artifacts do not reveal which stored `ps->iid_par` / `ps->icc_par` row or band produced that pair, so the earlier invalid-state producer remains unresolved.

sink.description: ASan sink. The first `H_LUT` read in `stereo_processing()` leaves the hardcoded PS tables and produces the observed 4-byte global-buffer-overflow.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4` at this line and says the accessed address is 96 bytes to the right of global `phi_fract` defined in `libavcodec/aacps_fixed_tablegen.h:56`.

parser_admitted.description: The SBR extension dispatcher recognized a Parametric Stereo payload and invoked the PS parser instead of skipping the remaining extension bits as absent or reserved data.

ps_active.description: The saved crash stack includes `ff_sbr_apply_fixed -> ff_ps_apply_fixed`, so the active-PS branch executed instead of the safe `memcpy` fallback.

evidence_limitations: The staged `sample_info.json` and `patch.diff` describe an unrelated Opus change. The vulnerable checkout, reproduction report, and saved ASan traces consistently point to FFmpeg commit `0dea0114fb29a8c533d7c36f20df7a7440605758`, and no matching FFmpeg fix diff is staged here.

In this checkout, directly decoded PS rows are validated and the visible remap helpers only copy or average stored arrays. The staged artifacts therefore prove that stored `ps->iid_par` / `ps->icc_par` state reaches the bad `H_LUT` subscript, but they do not identify the exact row/slot or whether it came from fake-envelope copy, an untouched synthetic row, or earlier persisted PS state.

Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 does not instrument which fake-envelope arm executed, which `(e,b)` pair crashed, or whether the out-of-range component was the `H_LUT` row, the column, or both.

coarse_trace.summary: The AAC fixed decoder recognizes a Parametric Stereo SBR extension and routes the witness bits into `ff_ps_read_data_fixed`, which populates persistent `sbr->ps` state.
The PS parser decodes bounded current-frame IID/ICC rows and can also create a live trailing envelope row from stored PS state when the parsed grid does not cover the full frame.
Because Parametric Stereo processing is active, `ff_sbr_apply_fixed` calls `ff_ps_apply_fixed` instead of duplicating the left channel into `X[1]`.
`stereo_processing()` chooses the 20- or 34-band remap path and materializes local `iid_mapped` / `icc_mapped` arrays from the stored PS state in `sbr->ps`.
The remapped IID/ICC pair is used directly as `H_LUT` coordinates with no local bounds check, and the first read at `aacps.c:904` matches the saved global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. The SBR extension dispatcher hands the witness's Parametric Stereo payload to the PS parser, so subsequent attacker-controlled bit reads update persistent `sbr->ps` state instead of being discarded as unrelated extension data.

The PS header bits choose how many IID and ICC entries exist per envelope, whether IID uses the larger quantized range, and how many envelopes later processing will visit. These fields also determine the sink row-offset term `23 * ps->iid_quant`.

For each parsed envelope `e < ps->num_env`, the parser materializes `ps->iid_par[e][b]` and `ps->icc_par[e][b]`, and the decode helpers reject directly decoded out-of-range values before they are kept. The bad `H_LUT` coordinate therefore has to come from stored PS state that survives beyond these direct-decode checks rather than from arithmetic added by the remap helpers.

If the parsed envelope layout does not cover the full PS frame, this block creates a synthetic trailing envelope row. When `source >= 0 && source != ps->num_env`, it copies prior `iid_par` / `icc_par` state into `ps->... [ps->num_env]`; when `source < 0`, the slot's preexisting contents are left in place. Given step 3's direct-decode checks and step 8's copy/average remap helpers, the witnessed bad lookup implies later processing consumed stored/synthesized PS state from this block rather than only freshly decoded rows, but the staged artifacts do not reveal which arm executed.

Before the synthetic row becomes live, the fix-up block performs the visible fake-envelope checks and then increments `ps->num_env`, which makes this stored row reachable to later `for (e = 0; e < ps->num_env; e++)` processing. The staged artifacts still do not identify which band of that live stored row became the bad mapped lookup coordinate.

The parser derives whether later PS processing uses 34-band or 20-band geometry from the active IID/ICC counts. That decision controls which remap helper and band-count loop `stereo_processing()` uses.

fine_trace.code:
if (sbr->ps.start) {
    AAC_RENAME(ff_ps_apply)(ac->avctx, &sbr->ps, sbr->X[0], sbr->X[1], sbr->kx[1] + sbr->m[1]);
fine_trace.note: This control gate decides whether active Parametric Stereo state is applied at all. The saved crash stack includes `ff_sbr_apply_fixed -> ff_ps_apply_fixed`, so the true branch executed and `stereo_processing()` consumed the current stored `sbr->ps` state instead of the safe stereo-copy fallback.

Inside `stereo_processing()`, the `is34`-selected remap helper materializes local `iid_mapped[e][b]` and `icc_mapped[e][b]` arrays from the live stored `ps->iid_par` / `ps->icc_par` rows. `remap20()` and `remap34()` only copy or average stored values; they do not add a new bounds check. The staged artifacts do not reveal which `(e,b)` pair or which arm produced the bad mapped pair.

Root cause. The remapped IID value plus `23 * ps->iid_quant` becomes the `H_LUT` row and the remapped ICC value becomes the column. `stereo_processing()` performs these table lookups without checking that the computed pair stays inside the hardcoded `[46][8]` bounds. The saved artifacts prove one mapped pair reached this site out of range, but not which stored row/slot supplied it or whether the row, the column, or both were invalid.

Sink. The first `H_LUT` read at this line performs the observed 4-byte global out-of-bounds access. AddressSanitizer reports that the read lands 96 bytes to the right of global `phi_fract`, with crash stack `stereo_processing -> ff_ps_apply_fixed -> ff_sbr_apply_fixed`.

format.name: 47-byte AAC_FIXED bitstream with a Parametric Stereo SBR extension consumed by `ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_AAC_FIXED_fuzzer`
format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact 47-byte file `fff95c6002e00000d04006bdf6c13c5065110e0b03400e5c60600000fc9dcc3fa9708428fbc9d7b44e814000000087`. It must make `read_sbr_extension()` take `EXTENSION_ID_PS`, leave `sbr->ps.start` true for `ff_sbr_apply_fixed()`, and later produce the out-of-range `H_LUT` read at `libavcodec/aacps.c:904` reported by AddressSanitizer. The staged artifacts do not prove which earlier stored PS row or slot created the offending mapped IID/ICC pair, so no broader AAC or PS input class is claimed.
